jp: バスが{なかなか|av-nakanaka}来[こ]ないので、歩[ある]いて行[い]くことにした。
en: The bus just wasn't coming, so I decided to walk.
why: なかなか + ない means 'not easily / takes a long time', here the bus is long overdue.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は暑[あつ]くて{なかなか|av-nakanaka}眠[ねむ]れない。
en: It's so hot tonight that I just can't get to sleep.
why: The expected result (sleep) does not come easily: なかなか + negative.

jp: この問題[もんだい]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}解[と]けません。
en: I just can't solve this problem.
why: なかなか + negative potential says it does not work out however long you try.

jp: 子[こ]どもが{なかなか|av-nakanaka}泣[な]きやまなくて、困[こま]りました。
en: My child wouldn't stop crying for ages and I was at a loss.
why: なかなか + negative expresses that the change takes a long time to happen.

jp: 人気[にんき]の店[みせ]で、なかなか予約[よやく]が{取[と]れない|av-nakanaka}。
en: It's a popular restaurant and reservations are hard to get.
why: なかなか in the 'not easily' sense must end in a negative: 取れない.

jp: 彼[かれ]は約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]になってもなかなか{来[こ]ない|av-nakanaka}。
en: The agreed time has come, but he still hasn't shown up.
why: The sense 'is slow to come' requires なかなか + a negative verb.

jp: 練習[れんしゅう]しても、なかなか結果[けっか]が{出[で]ない|av-nakanaka}。
en: Even though I practise, results are slow to come.
why: なかなか + ない: the result does not appear easily.

jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだのに、熱[ねつ]が{なかなか|av-nakanaka}下[さ]がらない。
en: Even though I took medicine, the fever won't go down.
why: The fever fails to drop for a long time: なかなか + negative.

jp: 電話[でんわ]が{なかなか|av-nakanaka}つながらなくて、いらいらした。
en: I couldn't get through on the phone for ages and got irritated.
why: なかなか + つながらない describes a connection that takes a long time to succeed.

jp: 朝[あさ]、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}起[お]きられなくて、よく遅刻[ちこく]します。
en: I can't manage to get up in the morning, so I'm often late.
why: なかなか + negative potential means 'can't easily do it'.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は人見知[ひとみし]りで、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}友達[ともだち]ができないそうだ。
en: She is shy, so apparently she doesn't easily make friends.
why: なかなか + ない shows the thing happens only with difficulty.

jp: 返事[へんじ]がなかなか{来[き]ません|av-nakanaka}。
en: The reply is taking a long time to arrive.
why: 'Slow to happen' needs なかなか + a negative ending (来ません).

jp: 夫[おっと]はなかなか{帰[かえ]ってこない|av-nakanaka}。
en: My husband is taking ages to come home.
why: The expected return keeps not happening, so なかなか + negative.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]が{なかなか|av-nakanaka}届[とど]かないので、店[みせ]に問[と]い合[あ]わせた。
en: The package wasn't arriving, so I contacted the shop.
why: A delivery that is long overdue is なかなか + 届かない.

jp: この漢字[かんじ]は、何度[なんど]書[か]いても{なかなか|av-nakanaka}覚[おぼ]えられない。
en: No matter how many times I write this kanji, I can't memorise it.
why: Repeated effort without result is なかなか + negative potential.

jp: 駐車場[ちゅうしゃじょう]は混[こ]んでいて、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}空[あ]いている場所[ばしょ]が見[み]つからなかった。
en: The car park was crowded and we couldn't find a free space for a long time.
why: なかなか + negative: the goal took a long time and was not reached easily.

jp: 彼[かれ]は頑固[がんこ]で、人[ひと]の意見[いけん]を{なかなか|av-nakanaka}聞[き]き入[い]れない。
en: He is stubborn and doesn't readily accept other people's opinions.
why: 'Does not easily accept' is なかなか + ない.

jp: 寒[さむ]くて、布団[ふとん]からなかなか{出[で]られない|av-nakanaka}。
en: It's so cold that I can't get out of my futon.
why: なかなか + 出られない says getting out is hard to do.

jp: 新[あたら]しい仕事[しごと]に{なかなか|av-nakanaka}慣[な]れません。
en: I can't seem to get used to my new job.
why: The change (getting used to it) is slow in coming: なかなか + negative.

jp: この店[みせ]のラーメンは{なかなか|av-nakanaka}おいしいですよ。
en: The ramen at this shop is quite good, you know.
why: なかなか + a positive evaluation means 'quite / rather good', a pleasant surprise.

jp: 初[はじ]めて描[か]いた絵[え]にしては、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}上手[じょうず]ですね。
en: For a first painting, it's rather good, isn't it?
why: Praise that is better than expected takes なかなか + a positive adjective.

jp: 先週[せんしゅう]見[み]た映画[えいが]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}面白[おもしろ]かったです。
en: The film I saw last week was quite interesting.
why: A positive judgement stronger than expected: なかなか + 面白かった.

jp: このホテルは古[ふる]いけれど、部屋[へや]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}きれいだ。
en: This hotel is old, but the rooms are quite clean.
why: なかなか + a positive adjective praises something above expectation.

jp: 彼[かれ]の英語[えいご]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}流暢[りゅうちょう]だった。
en: His English was quite fluent.
why: なかなか adds approving emphasis to a positive description.

jp: この小説[しょうせつ]は長[なが]いけれど、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}読[よ]みやすい。
en: This novel is long, but it is quite easy to read.
why: A positive adjective with a favourable surprise takes なかなか.

jp: 山[やま]の上[うえ]から見[み]る景色[けしき]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}美[うつく]しかった。
en: The view from the top of the mountain was quite beautiful.
why: なかなか + 美しかった is positive praise ('rather beautiful').

jp: 初心者[しょしんしゃ]なのに、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}いい点数[てんすう]を取[と]ったね。
en: For a beginner, you got quite a good score, didn't you?
why: Praise beyond expectation for a beginner: なかなか + いい.

jp: 駅[えき]から遠[とお]いけど、この部屋[へや]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}住[す]みやすいよ。
en: It's far from the station, but this room is quite comfortable to live in.
why: The positive evaluation is better than the drawback suggests: なかなか.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]の歌[うた]を聞[き]いて、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}やるなと思[おも]った。
en: Hearing her sing, I thought she was pretty good.
why: なかなかやる is a fixed way of praising someone as better than expected.

jp: その新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]は、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}教[おし]え方[かた]がうまい。
en: The new teacher is quite good at teaching.
why: なかなか + a positive skill: 'quite good at'.

jp: 子[こ]どもが作[つく]った料理[りょうり]にしては、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}いい味[あじ]だった。
en: For a dish a child made, it tasted quite good.
why: A favourable surprise ('for a child') is expressed by なかなか + positive.

jp: この公園[こうえん]は小[ちい]さいけれど、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}人気[にんき]があるそうです。
en: This park is small, but apparently it is quite popular.
why: なかなか + a positive description gives the sense 'quite / considerably'.

jp: 買[か]ったばかりの靴[くつ]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}はき心地[ごこち]がいい。
en: The shoes I just bought are quite comfortable to wear.
why: なかなか praises the comfort as better than expected.

jp: 君[きみ]の作文[さくぶん]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}よく書[か]けている。
en: Your essay is quite well written.
why: A teacher's approving comment: なかなか + a positive predicate.

jp: この辞書[じしょ]は{なかなか|av-nakanaka}使[つか]える。
en: This dictionary is quite useful.
why: なかなか使える is a common positive evaluation: 'rather good / handy'.

jp: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]の散歩[さんぽ]も、{なかなか|av-nakanaka}いいものですよ。
en: A walk on a rainy day is also quite nice, you know.
why: なかなかいい expresses unexpectedly good value.
